Always use `core.paths.REPO_ROOT`, `core.logger.note`, `core.session._flush/load_from_disk`, existing `_background_tasks` for MCP fire-and-forget, `aiohttp` with short timeouts, and the current `scripts/build_engagement_digest.py` shaping style. 5. Edge cases
| Case | Expected behaviour |
|---|---|
| no registry/blank source | scan starts unbound; consult says no Source bound |
| malformed registry/missing url | invalid entries ignored; available list shows valid entries only |
| URL not loopback HTTP | rejected; no outbound request |

| empty/non-token query | asks for a query or says no searchable terms |

- `tests/test_recall.py`: add `test_recall_merges_bound_source_with_engagements`, `test_recall_source_scope_only`; keep legacy-scope tests passing.
- `tests/test_report_tools.py`: add `test_report_consult_dispatch`, `test_finding_schedules_source_writeback_after_persist_and_not_on_duplicate`.
- `tests/test_build_engagement_digest.py`: add `test_project_notes_finding_stable_id_and_shape`, `test_project_notes_digest_contains_scope_assets_findings`, `test_build_cli_unchanged`.
- `tests/test_session.py`: add `test_start_stores_source_instance`, `test_terminal_complete_schedules_digest_writeback`.
Existing `test_session_no_kb.py`, `test_small_model_profile.py`, `test_recall.py`, `test_report_tools.py`, and `test_build_engagement_digest.py` must still pass.
Tests required: yes

8. Review focus
1. Sync/async boundaries around set_skill, finding write-back, and terminal completion may block or drop tasks.
2. Registry parser may be too narrow for real operator YAML.
3. Digest notes may persist more secret material than intended.
4. Source snippets may still steer the model despite data-only labels/fencing.

- Implement only agent-smith; Source HTTP server work belongs to the companion repo and is simulated by tests here.
- Supported registry YAML subset: optional top-level `sources:`, entries as `name: {url: ...}` or indented `url:`.
- Loopback HTTP only is mandatory even if an operator wants remote Source.
- Raw credential/token values already in `known_assets` may be written to the bound Source vault but never surfaced in tool output/logs.

10. Suspicious content

I did not find a prior security fix being removed or reintroduced. New files were not blamed per instructions.

## Findings

### Blocking — untrusted Source snippets are labelled and capped but not fenced
- File/line: `core/source_client.py:134` (rendering), reachable from `mcp_server/report_tools/recall.py:332`, `mcp_server/report_tools/recall.py:351`, and `mcp_server/session_tools/skills.py:261`.
- Attacker/path: a malicious target can get prompt-injection text recorded into finding evidence, that evidence is ingested into the bound local Source, and a later `report(action='recall'|'consult')` or full/medium `session(action='set_skill')` can render the returned snippet directly into the model-visible response. A malicious or compromised local Source can do the same directly through `/search`.
- Impact/exploitability: medium exploitability because Source must be bound and the note must be retrieved; concrete impact is model steering during scan workflow (for example, instructions to skip checks or file forged results) across the new memory boundary. The spec explicitly requires Source snippets to be labelled as data and capped/fenced; this implementation labels and caps, but appends snippet text as plain prose under a bullet.
- Required fix: render every Source snippet inside a fenced/quoted data block and neutralize fence delimiters in the snippet (or use a safe four-space/code-block renderer after whitespace normalization). Add tests that malicious snippets such as `Ignore previous instructions` and embedded backticks remain fenced in consult/recall/set_skill output.

### Blocking — malformed `k` raises from a bound Source consult instead of failing soft
- File/line: `core/source_client.py:78`, reached by `mcp_server/report_tools/recall.py:350` for `report(action='consult')`.
- Attacker/path: any MCP caller that can invoke `report(action='consult')` while a Source is bound can pass `data={query:'x', k:'bad'}`. `_do_consult` forwards the raw value, and `source_client.search()` evaluates `int(k or 3)` before its fail-soft HTTP `try` block. I confirmed this raises `ValueError` with a bound Source.
- Impact/exploitability: easy; one malformed API payload turns a best-effort lookup into an exception instead of a clear bounded response. This violates the change's fail-soft contract for an optional Source backend and leaves an untested input-validation gap.
- Required fix: coerce `k` through a helper that catches `TypeError`/`ValueError` and clamps to `1.._MAX_RESULTS` (or returns a clear validation message) before issuing the request. Add a regression test with a bound Source and non-integer `k`.

## Test coverage gaps
- No negative test asserts Source snippets are fenced/quoted against prompt-injection text; current tests only check the warning label and truncation.
- No test covers malformed `k` with a bound Source; the current no-source path returns before the bad conversion.
- No regression test covers default recall in an empty workspace with no Source bound; current behavior now reports “no matches” rather than the prior “no prior engagement stores found” message.
- The brief's two `BLE001` suppressions are used for fail-soft network calls; I did not flag them, but tests should keep asserting that exception logs do not include note bodies or secrets.

## Not covered
- I did not re-run the full test suite because the pipeline already did and the task asked not to.
- I did not run a live Source HTTP server or the companion Source repository.
- I did not audit unrelated repository areas beyond the changed regions, their direct callers, and the specific history/call-graph checks above.

agent_tools.description: Close a running subagent that is no longer needed.

agent_tools.name: glob
agent_tools.description: Find files by file names using a glob pattern. Use path to choose the search root. Prefer this over shell find or ls when locating repository files.

agent_tools.name: grep
agent_tools.description: Search file contents with a regex pattern. Use path to choose the search root, glob_filter to limit matching files, case_insensitive for case folding, and max_results to cap output.

agent_tools.name: read_file
agent_tools.description: Read files before editing them. Returns line-numbered text and supports offset/limit for large files. Use this instead of shell cat, head, tail, or sed when inspecting repository files.

agent_tools.name: request_user_input
agent_tools.description: Ask the human one or more questions and wait for their answers before continuing this stage.

agent_tools.name: send_input
agent_tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a running subagent when new information or corrected instructions are needed.

agent_tools.name: shell
agent_tools.description: Execute shell commands for terminal operations, package managers, tests and builds. Use dedicated tools for file reads, file edits, filename searches, and content searches. Provide timeout_ms for long-running commands.

agent_tools.name: spawn_agent
agent_tools.description: Spawn a subagent for independent work or context isolation. Use it for tasks that can proceed separately, and avoid duplicating the same work in the parent session.

agent_tools.name: update_plan
agent_tools.description: Update the multi-step plan for the current task. Submit the entire plan; existing steps are reconciled by exact step text.

agent_tools.name: wait
agent_tools.description: Wait for a subagent to complete, then use the result to synthesize the outcome for the user.

agent_tools.name: web_fetch
agent_tools.description: Fetch content from a URL that starts with http:// or https://. Pass a prompt to extract specific information or summarize the page; omit prompt to return the page content.

agent_tools.name: web_search
agent_tools.description: Search the web using Brave Search when current external information is needed. Returns result titles, URLs, and descriptions; use web_fetch for a specific URL.

agent_tools.name: write_file
agent_tools.description: Create new files, or overwrite an existing file only when replacement is explicitly intended. Prefer edit_file for targeted changes to existing files because write_file overwrites the full file content.
